raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Two Triton kernels used by Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next compute token offsets from an int32 `tl.program_id(0)`. With Qwen3.5-4B layouts, the offset exceeds 2^31 at >= **174,764 tokens** in `_layer_norm_fwd_1pass_kernel`, and at >= **209,717 tokens** in `_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate_kernel`. Wider models hit it sooner: about 131K tokens for Qwen3.5-27B. Past that, the kernel faults with `an illegal memory access was encountered`, or silently returns wrong values.

Chunked prefill normally hides this. However, for noncausal decision models (e.g. [`pplx-decider-v1.1-27b`](https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Perplexity/PPLX-Decider-v1.1-27B)), chunked prefill is disabled, so long prompts hit this.

## Modifications

- Cast the program id to int64 in both kernels
- Corresponding unit tests which can reproduce the 2 issues, and pass after the fixes

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs are bitwise identical below the overflow point. On 1xH100:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| pplx-decider-v1.1-27b, 125,684 tokens | correct | correct |
| pplx-decider-v1.1-27b, 139,965 tokens | server crashes | correct |

The end-to-end run used `--quantization fp8` so a 140K prefill fits on one H100. Activations and kernel layouts are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1xH100, Qwen3.5-4B layouts, µs:

| T | gated norm main / PR | fused QK main / PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1,024 | 53.9 / 55.0 | 31.9 / 32.0 |
| 8,192 | 86.9 / 87.0 | 204.8 / 205.0 |
| 131,072 | 1,269.8 / 1,269.9 | 3,213.1 / 3,219.3 |

Tested on a v0.5.22 build with main's sources; both kernels are unchanged between v0.5.22 and main.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No documentation change needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -106,7 +106,8 @@ def _layer_norm_fwd_1pass_kernel(
         tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()
 
     # Map the program id to the starting row of X and Y it should compute.
-    row_start = tl.program_id(0) * ROWS_PER_BLOCK
+    # int64: rows * stride overflows int32.
+    row_start = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * ROWS_PER_BLOCK
     group = tl.program_id(1)
 
     # Create 2D tile: [ROWS_PER_BLOCK, BLOCK_N]

@@ -64,7 +64,7 @@ def _fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate_kernel(
     WEIGHT_SHIFT: tl.constexpr = 1.0,
     EXPLICIT_ROPE_FMA: tl.constexpr = False,
 ):
-    token = tl.program_id(0)
+    token = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)  # token * stride_qg_t overflows int32
     head = tl.program_id(1)
     is_k = head >= NUM_Q_HEADS
     local_head = tl.where(is_k, head - NUM_Q_HEADS, head)

@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@
 from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
 
-register_cuda_ci(est_time=13, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=16, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
 
 
 @unittest.skipIf(not torch.cuda.is_available(), "Test requires CUDA")
@@ -200,6 +200,44 @@ def test_strided_gate_matches_contiguous_gate(self):
                     )
                     torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
 
+    def test_strided_gate_rows_past_int32_offset(self):
+        # Past 2**31 elements of the projection, the last rows must match the
+        # same rows normed alone.
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        num_qk_heads, num_v_heads, head_dim = 16, 32, 128
+        width = 2 * (num_qk_heads + num_v_heads) * head_dim
+        tokens = 2**31 // width + 2
+        required = tokens * (width + 2 * num_v_heads + 2 * num_v_heads * head_dim) * 2
+        if torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0] < required + (1 << 30):
+            self.skipTest("Requires about 8 GiB of free GPU memory")
+        qkvz = torch.randn(tokens, width, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        ba = torch.randn(tokens, 2 * num_v_heads, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        _, z, _, _ = qwen3_5_gdn_prefill_projection_views(
+            qkvz, ba, num_qk_heads, num_v_heads, head_dim, head_dim
+        )
+        x = torch.randn(
+            tokens * num_v_heads, head_dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"
+        )
+        weight = torch.randn(head_dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        n = 4096
+        actual = rms_norm_gated(
+            x=x,
+            weight=weight,
+            bias=None,
+            z=z,
+            norm_before_gate=True,
+            is_rms_norm=True,
+        )
+        expected = rms_norm_gated(
+            x=x[-n * num_v_heads :],
+            weight=weight,
+            bias=None,
+            z=z[-n:],
+            norm_before_gate=True,
+            is_rms_norm=True,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual[-n * num_v_heads :], expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
 from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
 
-register_cuda_ci(est_time=6, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=8, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
 
 
 def gemma_rmsnorm(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, eps: float) -> torch.Tensor:
@@ -190,6 +190,46 @@ def test_rejects_positions_and_map_apart(self):
                 with self.assertRaises(AssertionError):
                     self.call(positions, mrope_axis_map=axis_map_passed)
 
+    def test_tokens_past_int32_offset(self):
+        """Past 2**31 elements of the packed QKV projection, the last tokens must
+        match the same tokens run alone."""
+        num_q_heads, num_kv_heads, head_dim = 16, 4, 256
+        q_gate_dim = 2 * num_q_heads * head_dim
+        kv_dim = num_kv_heads * head_dim
+        width = q_gate_dim + 2 * kv_dim
+        tokens = 2**31 // width + 2
+        # qkv and cos_sin_cache in, then q, k and gate out.
+        required = tokens * (width + self.rotary_dim + q_gate_dim + kv_dim) * 2
+        if torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0] < required + (1 << 30):
+            self.skipTest("Requires about 9 GiB of free GPU memory")
+        qkv = torch.randn(tokens, width, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        q_weight = torch.randn(head_dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        k_weight = torch.randn(head_dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        cos_sin_cache = torch.randn(
+            tokens, self.rotary_dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        positions = torch.arange(tokens, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+
+        def run(rows):
+            return fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate(
+                qkv[rows, :q_gate_dim],
+                qkv[rows, q_gate_dim : q_gate_dim + kv_dim],
+                q_weight,
+                k_weight,
+                cos_sin_cache,
+                positions[rows],
+                self.eps,
+                num_q_heads,
+                num_kv_heads,
+                head_dim,
+                self.rotary_dim,
+                has_gate=True,
+            )
+
+        n = 4096
+        for out, tail in zip(run(slice(None)), run(slice(-n, None))):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(out[-n:], tail, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
